HYDRAULIC NARRATIVE: the bridge is first read as a river regime problem. The report therefore links cross-section, velocity, design discharge, afflux, scour and founding level in one continuous engineering story, so the subsequent pier and abutment checks are not detached from the flood model.
Design data: HFL = 100.600 m MSL, bed level = 96.600 m MSL, foundation level = 92.600 m MSL, Manning n = 0.033, bed slope = 1 in 960, total waterway = 96.00 m, and design discharge Q = 243.11 cumecs.

Step 1 - A) FLOW CALCULATION: the adopted waterway section gives area A = 141.500 m2 and wetted perimeter P = 60.773 m. Hence hydraulic radius R = A/P = 2.3283 m, velocity V = 1.718 m/s, and Froude number Fr = 0.274. The flow regime is read as Subcritical, so the discharge, afflux and scour computations are carried forward as one consistent hydraulic envelope.

Step 2 - B) WATERWAY, AFFLUX AND SCOUR: regime width is 74.841 m and the provided waterway exceeds the regime width requirement with provided/required ratio 1.283. Computed afflux is 0.256 m, design water level is HFL + afflux = 100.856 m MSL, and design scour depth is 4.800 m below the working bed. This fixes the foundation narrative before structural actions are accepted.
CHECK: for a submersible crossing, overtopping is intentional, but velocity is moderate; therefore drag, buoyancy, scour and anchorage remain governing review items. Hence O.K.

Design data: pier body 1.20 m x 3.50 m x 4.00 m; footing/base 2.50 m x 4.50 m x 1.00 m; base area A = 11.250 m2; pier cap 1.70 m x 4.00 m x 0.80 m.

Step 1 - A) DEAD LOAD CALCULATION: computed pier/substructure dead load = 420.00 kN. The load-case table applies dead-load factors from 1:1.00, 2:1.00, 3:1.00, 4:1.00, 5:1.35, so the restoring vertical load remains traceable in each service, flood, seismic and ultimate row.

Step 2 - B) LIVE LOAD CALCULATION: maximum generated live-load reaction on the pier line = 400.00 kN. Service case 1 uses live-load factor 1.00, while the ultimate case uses the governing live-load factor shown in the load table; this mirrors the legacy workbook's separate live reaction and moment disclosure before stress calculation.

C) LOADS DUE TO WATER CURRENT: hydraulic force is split into hydrostatic 310.985 kN plus drag/current 142.35 kN, giving total horizontal force 457.556 kN. Flood case 3 carries V = 244.638 kN, H = 453.335 kN, M = 643.153 kN-m, with buoyancy factor 1.00.

D) SEISMIC CONDITION: case 4 (Seismic Condition (DL+LL+Seismic)) is retained with DL factor 1.00, LL factor 0.25, buoyancy factor 1.00, V = 344.638 kN and M = 759.487 kN-m. If the site zone makes seismic non-governing, the report still states the checked row rather than hiding the decision.

E) WIND FORCE: pier wind screening force = 4.22 kN. Wind-factor cases are 2 (Construction Stage (DL+Wind)); 5 (Ultimate Limit State (ULS)), and the maximum wind-combination moment read from the generated table is 649.14 kN-m.

BASE PRESSURE CALCULATION: service base pressure q = V/A = 644.638 / 11.250 = 57.301 kN/m2. Governing bearing case 5 gives q = 88.146 kN/m2, while the footing pressure envelope reports qmax 194.507 kN/m2 and qmin -79.905 kN/m2 against SBC 150.00 kN/m2.

STABILITY VERDICT: governing sliding is case 3 with FOS 0.270; governing overturning is case 3 with FOS 0.856; governing bearing is case 5 with FOS 1.702. Compare against Sliding >= 1.50, Overturning >= 1.80, Bearing >= 2.50. Hence NOT O.K. - revise inputs/member sizes and re-verify.

Step 1 - A) DEAD LOAD CALCULATION: pier/self and deck reactions are accumulated into vertical restoring action. The current pier result carries dead load 420.00 kN and live load 400.00 kN, so every stability case starts from the same computed vertical load table used by the workbook.

Step 2 - B) LIVE LOAD CALCULATION: live load reaction is 400.00 kN and is activated by the service and ultimate combinations through live-load factors in the pier load-case table. This preserves the legacy workbook habit of keeping live reaction and braking/longitudinal effects visible before base stress is read.

C) LOADS DUE TO WATER CURRENT: hydrostatic force = 310.985 kN, drag/current force = 142.35 kN, buoyancy = 175.362 kN, and total horizontal action = 457.556 kN. These forces are applied with foundation lever arms to produce sliding, overturning and base-pressure checks.

D) SEISMIC CONDITION: the seismic-design row is case 4 (Seismic Condition (DL+LL+Seismic)) with V = 344.638 kN, H = 535.335 kN and M = 759.487 kN-m. The report keeps this row explicit even when seismic is not governing.
E) WIND FORCE: wind-sensitive combinations are case 2, case 5; maximum wind-combination moment carried by the load table is 649.14 kN-m and pier wind screening force is 4.22 kN.

BASE PRESSURE / EARTH PRESSURE LINK: Rankine Ka = 0.333 and active thrust Pa = 75.00 kN. Pa acts at approximately H/3 above base and is carried into abutment sliding, overturning and bearing verification, including surcharge where generated by the engine.

Step 1 - HYDRAULIC VERIFICATION: section, regime width, afflux and scour are checked as a mutually consistent chain. High-level bridges must satisfy freeboard/clearance; submersible bridges must state overtopping intent and then prove current, buoyancy and stability behavior.

Step 2 - STRUCTURAL VERIFICATION: governing pier and abutment load cases must keep sliding, overturning and bearing within acceptance. Cantilever/C1 minima are Sliding 0.976, Overturning 1.078, Bearing 2.823. Hence NOT O.K. - revise inputs/member sizes and re-verify.
A) DEAD LOAD CALCULATION REVIEW: pier/substructure dead load 420.00 kN is the base restoring component. Service case 1 carries V = 644.638 kN and q = V/A = 57.301 kN/m2 over base area 11.250 m2.

B) LIVE LOAD CALCULATION REVIEW: live reaction 400.00 kN is visible through the service and ultimate live-load factors. This preserves the attached workbook's practice of separating live reaction before combining moments and stresses.
C) LOADS DUE TO WATER CURRENT REVIEW: hydrostatic 310.985 kN plus drag/current 142.35 kN gives horizontal action 457.556 kN. Flood case 3 reports M = 643.153 kN-m and buoyancy factor 1.00.

D) SEISMIC CONDITION REVIEW: case 4 (Seismic Condition (DL+LL+Seismic)) remains in the audit table with V = 344.638 kN, H = 535.335 kN and M = 759.487 kN-m. A non-governing seismic result is still stated, not silently omitted.
E) WIND FORCE REVIEW: wind-factor cases are case 2, case 5 and pier wind screening force is 4.22 kN. Wind therefore remains part of the report audit trail even when water current controls.

BASE PRESSURE / STABILITY VERDICT: governing pier bearing case 5 gives q = 88.146 kN/m2; pier minima are Sliding 0.270, Overturning 0.856, Bearing 1.702. Hence NOT O.K. - revise inputs/member sizes and re-verify.

ABUTMENT / FOUNDATION VERIFICATION: Type1 minima are Sliding 0.976, Overturning 1.078, Bearing 2.823; C1 minima are Sliding 0.976, Overturning 1.078, Bearing 2.823. This extends the source PCC abutment workbook's sill/foundation/seismic pressure checks into the final report narrative.
